statement: Let a position be any byte slice of length between 1 and 60 whose bytes are all 43 or 45. Define the predicate Win(p) on positions by well-founded recursion on the number of '+' bytes in p: Win(p) is true if and only if there exists an index i with 0 <= i < len(p)-1 such that p[i] = p[i+1] = 43, and letting p' be the position obtained from p by replacing p[i] and p[i+1] with 45, we have Win(p') = false. (If no such i exists, Win(p) is false.) Whenever can_win(currentState) returns a result r, r is true if and only if Win(currentState) is true.
preconditions: The slice currentState has length between 1 and 60 inclusive. Every byte is either 43 (the ASCII code for '+') or 45 (the ASCII code for '-').

statement: For every input satisfying the preconditions, the function can_win returns a result (it does not panic, overflow, or go out of bounds).
preconditions: The slice currentState has length between 1 and 60 inclusive. Every byte is either 43 (the ASCII code for '+') or 45 (the ASCII code for '-').

statement: If there is no index i with 0 <= i < len(currentState)-1 such that currentState[i] = currentState[i+1] = 43, then whenever can_win(currentState) returns a result r, r = false.
preconditions: The slice currentState has length between 1 and 60 inclusive. Every byte is either 43 (the ASCII code for '+') or 45 (the ASCII code for '-').

statement: Whenever can_win(currentState) returns true, there exists an index i with 0 <= i < len(currentState)-1 such that currentState[i] = currentState[i+1] = 43, and if p' is the slice obtained from currentState by replacing positions i and i+1 with 45, then can_win(p') returns false.
preconditions: The slice currentState has length between 1 and 60 inclusive. Every byte is either 43 (the ASCII code for '+') or 45 (the ASCII code for '-').

statement: Whenever can_win(currentState) returns false, for every index i with 0 <= i < len(currentState)-1 such that currentState[i] = currentState[i+1] = 43, if p' is the slice obtained from currentState by replacing positions i and i+1 with 45, then can_win(p') returns true.
preconditions: The slice currentState has length between 1 and 60 inclusive. Every byte is either 43 (the ASCII code for '+') or 45 (the ASCII code for '-').

statement: If there exists an index i with 0 <= i < len(currentState)-1 such that currentState[i] = currentState[i+1] = 43, and if p' is the slice obtained from currentState by replacing positions i and i+1 with 45, and can_win(p') returns false, then can_win(currentState) returns true.
preconditions: The slice currentState has length between 1 and 60 inclusive. Every byte is either 43 (the ASCII code for '+') or 45 (the ASCII code for '-').

statement: If for every index i with 0 <= i < len(currentState)-1 such that currentState[i] = currentState[i+1] = 43, letting p' be the slice obtained from currentState by replacing positions i and i+1 with 45, we have that can_win(p') returns true, then can_win(currentState) returns false.
preconditions: The slice currentState has length between 1 and 60 inclusive. Every byte is either 43 (the ASCII code for '+') or 45 (the ASCII code for '-').

statement: Whenever both can_win(s) and can_win(s') return results, those results are equal.
preconditions: Let s be any byte slice of length between 1 and 59 inclusive, with every byte being 43 or 45. Let s' be the slice of length len(s)+1 obtained by prepending the byte 45 to s.

statement: Let s_rev be the slice of the same length as currentState such that s_rev[i] = currentState[len(currentState)-1-i] for all i. Whenever can_win(currentState) and can_win(s_rev) return results, those results are equal.
preconditions: The slice currentState has length between 1 and 60 inclusive. Every byte is either 43 (the ASCII code for '+') or 45 (the ASCII code for '-').
